title: Optimization of murine retinal mitochondrial injury model
author: Zhou, Fang, et al.
materials: Adult (8–10 weeks old) C57B6/J mice were anesthetized with pentobarbital (i.p. 60 mg/kg). Carbonyl cyanide 3-chlorophenylhydrazone (CCCP, CAS No.: 555-60-2, MCE) was diluted to 1.5 µg/µL,12.5 µg/µL,10 µg/µL, 7.5 µg/µL, 5 µg/µL,2.5 µg/µL with dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO, D2650, Sigma). A thirty-Gauge needle (Hamilton, USA) was inserted using a Hamilton microinjector (Hamilton Company, USA) toward the optic nerve 1 mm outside of the limbus under a microscope. The CCCP or DMSO were slowly injected after the needle tip was detected in the pupil area. A volume containing 1 μL of undiluted DMSO was intravitreally injected into the right eye, whereas a volume containing 1 μL of 1.5 µg/µL,12.5 µg/µL,10 µg/µL, 7.5 µg/µL, 5 µg/µL,2.5 µg/µL CCCP were intravitreally injected into the left eye. After 24 h, the mice were harvested, and the retinas were collected to extract total protein for western blotting. After 48 h, the mice were harvested, and Fresh eyeballs were collected for paraffin section and H&E staining (Fig. 1).Fig. 1Dose dependent effects of intravitreal injection of CCCP on the levels of Opa1 and p-Erk. (A) Representative western blotting of the levels of Opa1, p-Erk, Erk and tubulin for the indicated dosages of CCCP. (B) Quantitative changes of L-Opa1 for the indicated dosages of CCCP (One way ANOVA, P < 0.05). (C) Quantitative changes of P-Erk/Erk for the indicated dosages of CCCP (One way ANOVA, P < 0.05).Fig. 1

Freshly isolated retinas were soniccated in an ice-cold RIPA buffer (Beyotime, China), and protein concentrations were quantitated. Thirty to forty-five μg of protein per sample was separated by SDS-PAGE and then transferred onto PVDF membranes (Millipore, USA) for immunodetection. The membranes were incubated in the following antibodies: OPA1 (1:1000; Cell Signaling Technology; 67589), ERK1/2 (1:1000; proteintech; 16443-1-AP)

steps.title: Maintain mice under controlled conditions
steps.instruction: House adult C57B6/J mice (8–10 weeks old, 20–22 g) purchased from SPF (Beijing) Biotechnology under a 12 h light/12 h dark cycle with lights on at 8 AM.

steps.title: Anesthetize mice
steps.instruction: Inject pentobarbital intraperitoneally at 60 mg per kg body weight to achieve surgical anesthesia.

steps.title: Prepare CCCP and DMSO solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute carbonyl cyanide 3‑chlorophenylhydrazone (CCCP, CAS 555‑60‑2, MCE) in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO, D2650, Sigma) to final concentrations of 1.5 µg/µL, 12.5 µg/µL, 10 µg/µL, 7.5 µg/µL, 5 µg/µL, and 2.5 µg/µL. Keep undiluted DMSO as control.

steps.title: Perform intravitreal injections
steps.instruction: Using a 30‑gauge Hamilton needle attached to a Hamilton microinjector, insert the needle toward the optic nerve 1 mm outside the limbus under a microscope until the tip is visualized in the pupil area. Inject 1 µL of undiluted DMSO into the right eye (control) and 1 µL of each CCCP solution into the left eye of separate mice, delivering the volume slowly.

steps.title: Harvest retinas for western blot (24 h)
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours after injection, euthanize the mice and dissect the retinas for protein extraction.

steps.title: Harvest eyeballs for histology (48 h)
steps.instruction: Forty‑eight hours after injection, euthanize the mice and collect fresh eyeballs for paraffin embedding and H&E staining.

steps.title: Extract protein and run western blot
steps.instruction: Sonicate isolated retinas in ice‑cold RIPA buffer (Beyotime, China) and determine protein concentration. Load 30–45 µg of protein per lane, separate by SDS‑PAGE, and transfer onto PVDF membranes (Millipore, USA). Block and incubate membranes with primary antibodies: OPA1 (1:1000; Cell Signaling Technology, 67589) and ERK1/2 (1:1000; Proteintech, 16443‑1‑AP). Proceed with standard immunodetection.

steps.title: Prepare KW6002 solution
steps.instruction: Freshly dissolve KW6002 in a mixture of 15 % DMSO, 15 % Castrol oil, and 70 % water to achieve a final concentration of 0.3 mg/mL, as described previously.

steps.title: Process eyeballs for H&E staining
steps.instruction: Fix harvested eyeballs overnight in 4 % paraformaldehyde at 4 °C. Dehydrate through an ascending ethanol series, clear with xylene, embed in paraffin, and cut 5 µm sections. Dewax sections with xylene followed by a descending ethanol series, then stain with hematoxylin and eosin. Observe and photograph sections under a Leica confocal microscope.
